newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close up on selective blue chip buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close up on selective blue chip buying.

text.p: Malaysian equities closed higher on Wednesday as foreign institutional funds selectively bought main board stocks in quiet trading, dealers said.
"A lot of heavy-weight foreign funds are looking at Malaysia now, focusing on the mid-cap stocks," said Dominic Armstrong, head of research at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
The weighted Composite Index of 100 blue-chip stocks closed up 6.01 points to 1,202.09, posting a new high for 1996. The Second Board index ended down 2.34 to 638.93.
Magnum closed up 18 cents to 4.72. The stock had grossly underperformed the market recently, said Armstrong.
"Many (foreign) funds have been underweight to neutral on Malaysia. This is not sensible," said Armstrong.
"Foreign money has been coming into the market in small amounts. They have been buying stocks like Olympia and Magnum," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at SJ Securities.
Gaming shares Olympia closed up 17 cents to 2.37 ringgit, and Magnum ended the session up 18 cents to 4.72.

"The interest rate cycle here is about to enter a downward phase, so banking, property and auto stocks should begin to look attractive," said Faez. Motor distributor Tan Chong closed up eight to 4.54.
